title: Micro-slab zoning and live-patch KV reclamation strategy
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Ongoing production incidents and telemetry show elevated KV cache fragmentation under mixed sequence-length workloads and variable batching patterns. Continuous batching (variable batch sizes and opportunistic micro-batches) interacts poorly with large contiguous KV allocations because hot entries get interleaved with cold ones, producing long-lived holes that increase GPU memory pressure and force expensive full-compaction pauses.

Proposal: Introduce a micro-slab zoning allocator and a live-patch reclamation flow that minimizes global compaction. Key ideas: (1) Partition GPU KV memory into small, time-windowed zones (micro-slabs) that preferentially host entries with similar tenure and access frequency; (2) Track a lightweight "patch ledger" per zone to record relocations so we can perform in-place live patching during natural batching quiescence windows; (3) Opportunistically relocate low-score entries to host or compressed storage ahead of fragmentation thresholds; (4) Align micro-slab maintenance to batch boundaries using a low-latency maintenance worker so we avoid interference with tight tail-latency SLOs.

Goals: reduce full-compaction occurrences by >= 70%, decrease average GPU memory fragmentation ratio by 40%, and maintain 99th percentile token latency within existing SLOs during maintenance.

Constraints and tradeoffs: micro-slabs increase allocation metadata overhead; relocation adds extra host<->GPU traffic for low-score entries; placement policy must be inexpensive to evaluate in the request path. The approach prioritizes low-latency steady-state behavior over optimal absolute memory packing (we accept some slack in utilization for predictability).
design_decisions: Use fixed-size micro-slabs (configurable, default 256KB) so per-zone bookkeeping is bounded and cache-friendly.
Classify entries by short-term tenure buckets: transient (<1s), short (1s-60s), stable (>60s). Zone assignment biases toward tenure bucket to reduce churn.
Maintain a compact per-zone bitmap + rotation pointer to locate holes quickly without global scans.
Allow background live-patch relocation only during detected batch quiescence windows or when batch worker signals safe-maintenance token.
Eviction scoring uses composite metric: access frequency (exponential decay), last-access age, and batch-hotness (recently used in an active batch).
implementation_notes: Allocator: implement micro-slab manager in the runtime hot path with a fast-path for single-chunk allocations.
Patch ledger: append-only ring for relocation records per micro-slab; compacted asynchronously.
Relocation worker: GPU-side async kernel schedules copy and pointer patching; host-side fallback for large contiguous moves.
Batch integration: add a small API signal from batch scheduler to allocator (signal_quiescent_window(start_ts, duration_ms)).
Telemetry: expose per-zone fragmentation_ratio, relocations/sec, and maintenance_pause_ms to Console dashboards.
Fallback: if live-patch fails due to racing requests, fall back to short-lived shadow copy and atomic pointer swap with retry backoff.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests that simulate mixed seq-length workload show >=70% reduction in full global compactions compared to baseline.
Synthetic perf job preserves 99th percentile token latency within current SLO (no more than 5% regression) during maintenance windows.
Console telemetry surfaces per-zone metrics and an alert if relocation throughput drops below threshold.
Canary rollout run on dedicated small cluster for 48h with no memory OOMs and stable latency.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design doc posted to Confluence (link in artifacts). Starting spike to measure zone size sensitivity (Aisha).
2026-03-05: Spike results: 256KB micro-slab showed best compromise between metadata overhead and remapping granularity; recorded bench results and updated cost model.
2026-03-08: Prototype allocator implemented on dev branch (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5123). Basic allocation/bitmap works under unit tests.
2026-03-10: Integrations: added batch_quiescent API to batch scheduler; discovered race where very short batches (<10ms) cause noisy maintenance signals. Added minimum quiescence threshold.
2026-03-12: Telemetry hooks added to exporter; dashboard prototype at https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv-zones (internal). Preparing canary plan.
2026-03-13: Began internal canary on staging-dedicated-1 with 10% traffic. Observed 45% fewer compactions in first 12 hours; CPU for relocation worker within acceptable limits.
review_feedback: PM (Diego Rivera): prefer conservative defaults; make zone size and relocation thresholds runtime-configurable for Dedicated customers.
SRE (Maya Patel): require circuit-breaker that halts relocation if tail latency trends upward for 3 consecutive minutes.
Security (reviewed by Hannah Li): patch ledger must not expose identifiers; ledger entries should be encrypted in transit but stored only in memory (no disk persistence).
Design (Eve Laurent): consider UX in Console to show 'relocation pressure' per customer and allow manual pause/resume for enterprise ops teams.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: excessive host<->GPU transfer during mass relocations could starve inference kernels. Mitigation: throttle relocation worker and prioritize small-chunk moves during peak load.
Risk: metadata overhead increases memory footprint. Mitigation: benchmark micro-slab sizes and add compacted metadata representation for low-memory devices.
Risk: race conditions during pointer swap. Mitigation: implement atomic pointer swaps with short backoff and fallback to shadow-copy flow.

Run 72h canary on Dedicated cluster with customer-like workload (PM + SRE) — 4d
